key_insight: A large cross-cohort serum proteomics study identified 19 circulating proteins linked to ALS survival, with GSN and IGFBP2 adding prognostic value beyond standard clinical factors and neurofilament light chain.
clinical_relevance: These blood-based protein markers could help stratify ALS patients by risk and improve prognosis-focused clinical trial design and future precision-medicine approaches.
method: Analyzed serum from 741 ALS patients across independent cohorts in Israel and the UK.
Used two orthogonal proteomics platforms: mass spectrometry and Olink proximity extension assay (PEA).
Looked for proteins with concordant survival associations across cohorts and platforms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 19 proteins associated with survival across two independent cohorts measured on complementary proteomic technologies, with GSN and IGFBP2 improving survival prediction over clinical covariates and serum NfL.
watch_item: These are prognostic associations rather than validated clinical tests, so broader external validation and standardized assay implementation are still needed.
paper_title: Circulating protein profiling identifies prognostic biomarkers in amyotrophic lateral Sclerosis
